specification_compliance: No findings were listed to verify, so no verification records are returned.

I2: the library replaces worksheet._columns with a slice (`e._columns=e._columns.slice(0,a+1)` in @js-preview/excel 1.7.14 lib/index.js line 36). It does not truncate the array in place, so the array held in keepColumns (excelAdapter.ts:143) still has every defined column, and applyColumns (excelAdapter.ts:221) puts it back.

Sheet/record alignment: the library's Og iterates workbook.eachSheet and pushes one sheet per worksheet. beforeTransformData pushes one record per eachSheet call (excelAdapter.ts:237-243), so records[i] matches sheets[i] in transformData (excelAdapter.ts:256).
I3: font.size × 16/9, divided by the library's 1.333333 and rounded, gives Math.round(p × 4/3) for half-point sizes. Then +0.01 is added once per font object (excelAdapter.ts:196-207).
I5/I7: Sets keyed by font, column and range object prevent double scaling within one drawing. Each try/catch around the scaling is empty and nothing in the adapter writes to console.
INDEX.md:334-335 sets SPEC-CORE-167 to superseded and SPEC-CORE-168 to approved.
potential_unspecified_behavior: scaleColumns calls worksheet.getColumn(i) up to the widest row cellCount, and ExcelJS getColumn creates Column objects. As a result, worksheet._columns after preview can hold columns that the workbook did not define, set to the default width / 6. I2 says _columns holds 'every column object the worksheet defined'. The extra objects are consistent with the drawn widths but are not strictly 'defined' columns.
records in createSheetSizing is never reset. If the library ever called beforeTransformData more than once per instance, indices would misalign. drawExcel calls preview only once.
regression_risks: The adapter relies on @js-preview/excel 1.7.14 internals: the beforeTransformData call order, the size/1.333333 rounding, the _columns slice, and reading _columns[n].width × 6 in picture placement. A library upgrade could silently change the sizes.
test_coverage: FilePreview.excelActualSize.test.tsx has a fake whose getColumn creates columns like ExcelJS and whose conversion replaces _columns with a slice (lines 195-197, 291-292). It asserts the restored _columns length and widths (lines 860-952) and the beforeTransformData font scaling (line 974).
